changes: The canonical bucket table now uses existing BaseAllocator::common().allocate_optimal_raw and matching free_raw_nullable ownership instead of a private std::alloc payload.
Raw bucket heads are initialized before any link is changed, and old bucket memory is released before committing the new modulus.
A null table release remains a no-op without lazily allocating a common-allocator handle.
Node global Box ownership and open PackedWord transactional scratch are unchanged.

observations: allocation then Free order, including native Free(nullptr)
no allocation/free on nonempty no-growth requests
exact old/new modulus, extent, packed-node count and allocated flag
exact ordered bucket, mask and occupied-bit triples
node identities retained through successful rehash and injected failure
table identity retained on failure and no-op, replaced on success

fault_injection.native: The executable interposes Standard::AllocateOptimal and Standard::Free. Successful calls still use malloc/free. An enabled allocation boundary throws integer17 before malloc; null-return failure and host exhaustion are never executed.
fault_injection.rust: A cfg(test) thread-local private observer throws before the raw allocator call, outside GlobalAlloc. The observer is restored by an RAII guard. Exact allocation-boundary events and pre/post map snapshots are compared with the native fixture.
fault_injection.scope: This proves failure-before-mutation and successful release ordering at the allocator seam. It does not claim that a NATIVE malloc failure raises a catchable exception.
fault_injection.actual_null_policy: Pinned Standard::AllocateOptimal returns unchecked malloc result and ReSize immediately memset()s it. Rust retains handle_alloc_error for a rejected representable request; fatal behavior/signals are not asserted equivalent.

ownership_proof: The table retains exactly the raw payload pointer returned by the common policy, initializes every pointer slot, destroys nodes before release and frees the same raw payload once. Strict Miri validates allocation headers, pointer alignment/provenance, moves, rehash and destructor paths.

miri_exclusions.reason: Only the prior six positive libc-backtrace iterator tests are cfg(not(miri)); all six new bucket-policy tests, all30 raw-storage tests and all264 original tests run under strict Miri.

bindings.scope: Bucket allocation/release policy and pre-mutation failure boundary only; signed overload delegates to size_t path and its input conversion is covered by unchanged original/method/alias regressions. No global API completion credit.

remaining_gaps: The destination-index Vec remains an extra Rust rehash allocation: it computes all custom PackedWord hashes before rewiring to preserve the existing strong unwind guarantee. Removing it requires a sound native-primitive fast path or an explicitly specified custom-word unwind contract.

Common raw allocations use the existing layout-recovery header, so physical heap request size and custom global-allocator callbacks differ from native malloc. Alternate OCCT memory-manager configurations are not covered.
True null-allocation fatal behavior/signals and overflowing native bucket-byte arithmetic are not reproduced; no host exhaustion was attempted.
C++ container ABI, compiler array cookies and broad inventory reconciliation remain separate; no global ledger changes or full-class parity claim.
